title: A simulated-covariate bias analysis by STC and by MAIC
question: Is a MAIC version of the simulated-covariate bias analysis infeasible or too imprecise, as its authors assumed when restricting it to STC?
design: Unanchored transport with an unmeasured binary covariate imputed from its assumed relations; STC and MAIC sensitivity curves over the assumed target prevalence, with feasibility and effective sample size. 2 cells, 500 replicates each.
answer: The MAIC extension of the simulated-covariate bias analysis was feasible in at least 99.8% of replicates across assumed target prevalences from 0.1 to 0.9, lost effective sample size to 85 to 109 of 300 only at the extreme, and had a reported SE 3% to 14% above STC's. Both routes were unbiased. The restriction to STC was conservative rather than necessary. Both routes' multiply imputed intervals widened along the sweep more than the estimate's real spread (SE up to 0.28 against about 0.13), so coverage exceeded nominal.
findings: Refuting sentence holds: feasibility 0.998 to 1.000; MAIC SE / STC SE 1.03 to 1.14.
Effective sample size 85 to 231 of 300 along the sweep.
Bias at most 0.009 for both routes; coverage 0.956 to 1.000 (conservative toward the extremes).
not_answered: One binary unmeasured covariate, correct assumed relations, unanchored A side only, no decision reading. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: A's marginal log odds in a target with the assumed prevalence of the unmeasured covariate
n_sim: 500 per scenario, 1,000 in total, each over a 5-point sweep with 10 imputations
